title: Esther Martinez Native American Languages Programs Reauthorization Act
official_summary:
Esther Martinez Native American Languages Programs Reauthorization Act

This bill revises a grant program administered by the Administration for Native Americans at the Department of Health and Human Services to preserve Native American languages. The minimum number of enrollees in educational programs funded by grants is reduced from 10 to 5 enrollees in Native American language nests, which provide instruction through the use of a Native American language for children under the age of 7 and their parents. For survival schools, which are programs striving for fluency in a Native American language and proficiency in other academic fields, the minimum number of enrollees is reduced from 15 to 10. The bill increases the maximum duration of grants.

The program is reauthorized through FY2024.

summary.headline: Reauthorizes and adjusts a federal grant program that funds Native American language preservation, lowering minimum enrollment numbers and extending grant length through fiscal year 2024.
summary.what_it_does: This law renews a Department of Health and Human Services grant program run by the Administration for Native Americans that helps preserve Native American languages. It lowers the minimum number of students required for funded language nests, which teach children under 7 and their parents through a Native American language, from 10 to 5. It also lowers the minimum for survival schools, which aim for fluency in a Native American language along with other academic subjects, from 15 to 10. The law allows grants to last longer and keeps the program authorized through fiscal year 2024.

who_it_affects.group: Native American tribes and communities running language nests
who_it_affects.how: Language nests can now qualify for grant funding with as few as 5 enrollees instead of 10.
Survival schools can qualify for grant funding with as few as 10 enrollees instead of 15.

who_it_affects.group: Young children under 7 and their parents in language nest programs
who_it_affects.how: Smaller programs can now receive funding, which may make language nests available in more communities.

who_it_affects.group: Organizations that receive Administration for Native Americans grants
who_it_affects.how: Grants can now run for a longer period under the revised rules.
